The Research Assistant or Research Analyst will help the Regulatory Affairs and Legal Research team monitor and analyze proposed regulatory actions, research policy and regulatory issues in connection with the drafting of public comments, and track legal and policy developments. The Research Assistant or Research Analyst will also help develop and maintain the Regulatory Affairs and Legal Research team’s data systems and support the team’s collaboration with key stakeholders and partners outside the organization. This position is full-time. Democracy Forward’s office is located in Washington, DC. While this position offers flexibility to work remotely, it requires regular in-office presence eight (8) times per month (averaging 2 times per week). Remote candidates within the United States will also be considered. If a candidate is outside of the DC area, travel to DC is expected 1–2 times per quarter. The application deadline for this role is Thursday September 17 at 11:59pm ET. Key Responsibilities: Below are the key areas of responsibility for this role. The specifics of each responsibility may vary based on the needs of the organization and department. Monitor and track federal regulatory activity, including proposed rules, executive actions, and other administrative actions. Help analyze proposed rulemakings and administrative actions to identify opportunities for engagement. Conduct policy, regulatory, and social science research to support the Regulatory Affairs and Legal Research team’s work in connection with public comments and other regulatory submissions. Analyze and synthesize data related to federal regulatory actions. Assist in coordinating timely responses to regulatory actions, including client and partner engagement. Support the Regulatory Affairs and Legal Research team’s efforts to build and maintain relationships with partner organizations, policy experts, and external stakeholders. Experience managing data projects and research functions. Experience working on teams in a collaborative structure. Demonstrated excellence in organizational and communication skills. Excellent writing skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple, competing deadlines and priorities. Commitment to democracy and social progress.
